name: Enjoei
tagline: Brazilian peer-to-peer marketplace for secondhand clothes, shoes and assorted stuff, with a deliberately goofy voice.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Listing is free, the platform earns a seller commission plus payment and shipping fees, so there is no monthly number to quote.

verdictSummary: The software here is the boring part: listings, search, chat, checkout, escrow, shipping labels. What you cannot build is a few million Brazilians who already show up looking for a used Zara dress in size 38. A one-shot clone gives you a beautiful empty mall. Even if you only want the seller side, the buyers, the payment escrow, the Correios integration and the dispute process all live on their side of the fence.
coreLoopDIY: A local inventory and listing manager for your own secondhand stuff: photos, measurements, drafted listing copy, where each item is posted, what it sold for and your actual margin after fees and shipping.
requirements: Node and a local database, nothing else
Optional: an LLM API key if you want auto-drafted listing copy
whatYouLose: Buyers. All of them. This is the entire product.
Escrow and payment handling, so you are back to arranging transfers with strangers
Shipping label generation and tracking integration
Dispute resolution and the trust that comes from a platform standing behind a sale
Search and discovery: nobody is browsing your personal closet by brand and size
moatNotes: Two-sided liquidity in a specific country, in a specific category, with payments and logistics welded on. Regional secondhand marketplaces are unusually sticky because shipping costs and payment rails are local.
whyPeopleStillPay: Sellers hand over a commission because the alternative is shouting into Instagram stories and negotiating pix transfers with people who ghost. The platform brings someone who is already in buying mode, handles the money so neither side has to trust the other, prints the shipping label, and absorbs the fight when the package shows up wrong. That bundle is worth a cut of the sale, and none of it is a software problem you can solve alone.
notes: You can clone the listing UI before lunch and still have sold nothing by dinner. The moat is liquidity: Brazilian buyers who already search there, plus the payment escrow and shipping rails nobody wants to rebuild.
prompt:
Build a local-only secondhand selling tracker called "Closet Ledger". This is NOT a marketplace clone: there are no buyers, no checkout, no public site.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/closet.db, schema created on boot
- Local image storage in ./data/uploads, served through a route handler
- Single user, no auth, no accounts, no telemetry, runs on localhost

Data model:
- Item: title, category, brand, size, condition (new / like-new / used / worn), color, measurements (free text), acquisition cost, asking price, status (draft / listed / reserved / sold / withdrawn), notes
- Photo: belongs to an item, ordered, one marked cover
- Listing: belongs to an item, platform name (free text string, user typed), url, date listed, current price
- Sale: belongs to an item, sale price, platform fee, shipping cost paid by me, date, buyer handle (free text)

Features, in scope:
- Item list with filters by status, category, brand, size, and a text search
- Item detail page with drag-to-reorder photo upload, resized to max 1600px on upload with sharp
- A "draft listing copy" button that produces a title and description from the item fields using a simple template, plus an optional LLM rewrite if OPENAI_API_KEY is set in .env (skip the button silently if it is not)
- Copy-to-clipboard for the generated title and description
- A ledger view: total spent, total sold, net margin per item and overall, after fees and shipping
- CSV export of all items and sales

Explicitly out of scope: publishing to any marketplace, payments, shipping labels, any API that requires a marketplace account.

Deliver a README with setup in three commands, a .env.example containing only OPENAI_API_KEY, and seed data of five fake items so the UI is not empty on first run.
